Entering among God's servants has only a broad devotional overlap with the focus's servant who returns.

Abundant rain sent from heaven is a limited beneficial counterpart to the focus's heavenly intervention.

God holds the heavens and earth lest they collapse; this states the sustaining power presupposed by the focus's conditional threat.
The catalog of punishments includes both swallowing by the earth and destruction from above, closely matching the focus's two-directional warning.
The sky and earth stand only by God's command, making their apparent stability contingent in precisely the way the focus warns.
The earth in God's grasp and the heavens folded in His hand give a concentrated image of the absolute cosmic power behind the focus.
It directly commands people to look at what is in the heavens and earth, exposing the same refusal to recognize surrounding signs.
The call to consider the dominion of the heavens and earth, with a possibly near term, strongly develops the focus's warning through cosmic observation.

The folding of the sky on the Day of Judgment gives an eschatological counterpart to the focus's threat of heavenly disruption.
The earth's violent shaking is a direct realization of the instability the focus says God can impose.
The earth's final quake develops the focus's warning that the ground beneath people is not independently secure.
The trembling earth and collapsing mountains give a judgment-day version of the focus's threatened terrestrial upheaval.
The removal of mountains and exposure of the earth makes the created ground visibly subject to divine reordering.
God scatters the mountains and leaves the earth level, providing another concrete form of terrestrial transformation.
The sky's splitting in response to its Lord gives an end-time image of the heavenly vulnerability invoked in the focus.
The earthquake that seizes Thamud is a historical realization of destructive movement from the earth below.
The earthquake that destroys Shuayb's people reinforces the focus's warning against feeling secure on the earth.
The overwhelming cry that seizes the wrongdoers supplies a historical judgment context for the focus's conditional threat.
The overturned settlement and stones sent upon it show divine judgment arriving through a transformed earthly and heavenly order.
The earthquake that seizes Shuayb's deniers provides another narrative instance of the ground's destructive instability.

The earthquake that seizes Thamud adds a direct historical consequence for rejecting divine warning.

Firm mountains are set in the earth lest it shake with people, directly clarifying the contingency of the ground beneath them.
The sky is a protected roof whose signs many turn away from, closely linking the focus's sky to heedless refusal of divine evidence.
God brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and earth and knows what is concealed, extending the focus's all-surrounding cosmic field.

God makes the earth a settled place and the sky a structure, supplying the stable-order background to the focus's warning of reversal.
The creation and provisioning of the earth establish the domain that the focus says can be overturned by divine will.
The heaven's obedient response to divine command clarifies that the sky in the focus is fully subject to that command.
The earth contains signs for those of certainty, reinforcing the focus's invitation to recognize visible evidence.
The building and expansion of the heaven display the same divine mastery over the upper realm invoked in the focus.
The spreading of the earth makes its habitable order a deliberate act, not an independent guarantee of security.
The layered heavens are presented for repeated inspection, a direct counterpart to the focus's command to look at the sky.
The sequence of looking at the sky, mountains, and earth gives a concentrated observational program parallel to the focus's appeal to see.
